# 7-Day Budget Meal Plan for 4 Adults

A $120 weekly food budget is workable with simple staples, repeat ingredients, and a few flexible meals. I’m assuming a standard U.S. grocery store, pantry basics already on hand, and that the vegetarian person will eat the same meals with plant-based swaps.

## Grocery List and Budget Breakdown

| Item | Est. Cost | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Rice, 10 lb | $9 | Base for bowls, sides, and dinners |
| Pasta, 4 lb | $6 | Lunches and one dinner |
| Old-fashioned oats, 2 large tubs | $7 | Breakfasts |
| Bread, 4 loaves | $12 | Toast, sandwiches, French toast |
| Tortillas, 4 packs | $10 | Wraps, quesadillas, tacos |
| Eggs, 5 dozen | $15 | Breakfasts, fried rice, baking |
| Milk, 4 gallons | $14 | Cereal/oats, cooking, drinks |
| Peanut butter, 2 jars | $6 | Breakfast and snacks |
| Jelly or jam, 1 jar | $3 | Sandwiches and toast |
| Bananas, 2 bunches | $4 | Breakfast and snacks |
| Apples, 3 lb bag | $5 | Snacks and lunch sides |
| Frozen mixed vegetables, 8 bags | $16 | Easy sides, rice bowls, pasta |
| Potatoes, 10 lb | $7 | Roasted, mashed, breakfast hash |
| Onions, 3 lb | $4 | Flavor base for most meals |
| Carrots, 2 lb | $3 | Sides, soup, snacks |
| Canned beans, 10 cans | $10 | Vegetarian protein, chili, tacos |
| Canned tomatoes, 6 cans | $6 | Pasta sauce, chili, soup |
| Chicken thighs, 10 lb | $18 | Main protein for non-vegetarian meals |
| Shredded cheese, 2 lb | $10 | Quesadillas, pasta, potatoes |
| Lettuce or cabbage, 2 heads | $4 | Salads, wraps, taco topping |
| Seasonings/oil allowance | $6 | Salt, pepper, garlic powder, cooking oil |

**Estimated total: $135** if bought exactly as listed.

To fit closer to **$120**, use one of these adjustments:
- Reduce chicken thighs to 6–7 lb: save about $7–$8
- Drop 1–2 bags of frozen vegetables: save about $2–$4
- Buy 1 gallon less milk: save about $3–$4
- Use more beans and eggs for protein: save about $4–$6

**Adjusted target total: about $119–$122**

## 7-Day Meal Plan

### Day 1
**Breakfast:** Oatmeal with banana and peanut butter
**Lunch:** Bean and cheese quesadillas with lettuce
**Dinner:** Chicken, rice, and mixed vegetables; vegetarian version with beans instead of chicken

### Day 2
**Breakfast:** Eggs and toast with fruit
**Lunch:** Peanut butter and jelly sandwiches, carrots, apples
**Dinner:** Pasta with tomato sauce and vegetables; add chicken to one half of the pan if desired

### Day 3
**Breakfast:** Oatmeal with sliced apples and cinnamon
**Lunch:** Rice bowls with beans, cheese, and sautéed onions
**Dinner:** Baked potatoes with broccoli/mixed vegetables and cheese; add chicken on the side for non-vegetarians

### Day 4
**Breakfast:** Scrambled eggs, toast, banana
**Lunch:** Leftover pasta with vegetables
**Dinner:** Bean chili over rice; optional chicken served separately

### Day 5
**Breakfast:** Peanut butter toast and milk
**Lunch:** Chicken wraps for most, bean wraps for vegetarian
**Dinner:** Fried rice with eggs, vegetables, and onions; add chicken to one portion only

### Day 6
**Breakfast:** Oatmeal with banana
**Lunch:** Tuna is not included to avoid shellfish confusion, so use egg salad sandwiches or bean salad wraps
**Dinner:** Sheet-pan chicken thighs with potatoes and carrots; vegetarian plate gets potatoes, carrots, and beans

### Day 7
**Breakfast:** Eggs, toast, and fruit
**Lunch:** Leftover rice bowls with beans and vegetables
**Dinner:** Pasta night with tomato sauce, cheese, and vegetables; optional chicken on the side

## Simple Prep Schedule

### Sunday Prep
- Cook a big pot of rice for 2–3 days
- Hard-boil 12 eggs for breakfasts and lunches
- Chop onions, carrots, and lettuce/cabbage
- Bake or roast 4–5 lb of potatoes
- Mix a large pot of bean chili or bean tomato sauce
- Portion chicken into meal-size bags if frozen

### Midweek Prep
- Cook another pot of rice or pasta
- Roast remaining potatoes and carrots
- Refill chopped vegetables for wraps and salads
- Make a second batch of bean filling or egg salad
- Bake remaining chicken for 2 dinners

### Daily Routine
- Breakfast: 10–15 minutes
- Lunch: 10 minutes using leftovers or assembly meals
- Dinner: 25–40 minutes, with one sheet pan or one pot when possible

## Cost-Saving Notes

- Use beans and eggs as the main protein for the vegetarian meal portions.
- Keep dinners “base + topping” style so one meal works for everyone.
- Repeat ingredients on purpose: rice, beans, potatoes, eggs, tortillas, and pasta stretch the budget best.
- Buy store brands and frozen vegetables for the lowest cost per serving.

## Quick Actions
